brewing.notes: A safe starting point for oolong: gongfu style with water just off the boil.

description:
A hand-pounded lemon tea drink associated with Guangdong; it is a recipe rather than a leaf.

This is a way of preparing tea more than a tea you buy under one name, so the recipe and the base tea change from one maker to the next.
history: The name literally means hand-beaten lemon tea. Little is documented about it.
processing: Made from a oolong base tea according to the recipe; the method varies.
harvest_season: Not tied to a harvest: it depends on the base tea.
appearance_dry: Usually twisted strips or rolled balls, from green to dark brown depending on the roast.
appearance_liquor: Usually from golden to amber, depending on oxidation and roast.
appearance_wet: Usually whole leaves that open up, often with darker edges.
taste_profile: Expect what oolongs usually give: floral or fruity notes, more roasted when the leaf is roasted.
vintage_note: Not sold by vintage: it is made from whatever base tea the maker keeps, so freshness of the base matters more than the year.
